newsitem.title: USA: Atlanta Fed's Guynn sees demand for US debt.
newsitem.headline: Atlanta Fed's Guynn sees demand for US debt.

text.p: Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta Jack Guynn said on Monday that foreign investors will continue to be a source of demand for U.S. government securities.
In a question and answer period following an address to the Atlanta Rotary Club, Guynn said he was "not terribly concerned" about the strength of foreign demand for U.S. government securities.
Guynn said the attractiveness of U.S. debt relative to other investment options that foreign investors might have could be more or less at a given time.
"But given world financial markets, the way they operate today, there will be takers for U.S. debt assuming we continue to manage our economy in a reasonable way," Guynn said.
Guynn said he does not see huge upswings in the economies of European nations in 1997.
"The prospects next year in aggregate are modest," he said. "We're not looking for a huge upswing in the economies of our European trading partners this year."
Guynn said the government's key inflation measure, the Consumer Price Index (CPI), had some biases, "most of them overstating (the level of inflation), but some clearly understating it."
He said it would probably take "a couple of years" to make any adjustments to the CPI.
Guynn also said federal government debt relative to the size of the U.S. economy is "relatively low" compared to some other major nations.
"However," he said, "as long as we've got the kind of debt that we've got, we are not optimizing economic performance in this country.
"Most of the (research) work that's been done suggests that the current levels of debt are clearly detrimental to the long-term health of the U.S. economy," Guynn said.
